name: TOTP Recovery Code Rotation Success
summary: An authenticated user with TOTP enabled explicitly chooses to replace the current recovery-code set, confirms the destructive rotation, and receives the newly issued recovery codes on the dedicated recovery-code surface.
finalOutcome: TOTP remains enabled for the current durable identity, all previously issued recovery codes are invalidated, and a fresh recovery-code set is displayed to the user.

sourceReferences.note: RotateRecoveryCodesAsync replaces the stored recovery-code secret and returns the fresh plaintext codes while leaving TOTP enabled.
Recovery-code rotation is modeled separately from TOTP disable because the durable MFA post-state is materially different.

Authored test design has started. Server proof must exercise the real MFA manager through a normalized authentication flow/handler path, prove the previous recovery-code set is invalidated, prove a fresh set is returned while TOTP remains enabled, and capture TotpRotateRecoveryCodesStart/TotpRotateRecoveryCodesSuccess transition evidence. Runtime setup must establish real TOTP and recovery-code material before this behavior can be independently executed.
